problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.000\,6$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
64,\,32,\,16,\,8,\,…
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.004$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
20,\,4,\,\frac{4}{5},\,\frac{4}{25},\,…
$$

The first term that is less than $0.004$ is the
{{field-1}}th term.
feedback.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=20$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =20{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $0.004.$
Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & <0.004 \\ 20{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} & <0.004 \\ {(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} & <\frac{0.004}{20} \\ \operatorname{log}⁡{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,2) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{5}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,2) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,2)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{5})} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,2)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{5})}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we reversed the inequality sign when divided by $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{5})$ because $\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{5})$ is a negative number. 

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,2)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{1}{5})}+1≈6.292.
$$

Therefore, the $7$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $0.004.$
